beats.headline: Tutorial Guild Hall, first floor
beats.text: Rule one: I don't open the door until you kill a goblin. The cat desecrates my mother. The man blows up a Murder Dozer. I open the door. My name is Mordecai. Borant holds my indenture, which means I guide for the first three floors and run a magic guild after that, where they mostly leave me alone to brew and look up old friends. Try to live long enough for that to matter.

beats.headline: The seventh or eighth human world
beats.text: When I signed on as a guildmaster they rebuilt my home for me, possessions and all. I had a few moments to grab what I wanted before they evaporated the rest. Every new world, they change my shape. Always some mob from the current floor. I don't know why. This is the seventh or eighth human-seeded world I've worked, kid, and it's always the same. You humans want to know why. My people last longer than yours. You know why? We roll with it.

beats.headline: This is my last tour
beats.text: I've been preparing for this world longer than you've been alive. Entered the prep phase in your 1964. Once got to wear a human shape and stole James Bond tapes from a Blockbuster. This is my last tour. When it's over I'm a full citizen with a moderate stipend. My home planet is not open to me. Ask about the ones who stayed up top and we get back to the tutorial. I made it to eleven, saw what guarded the stairs to twelve, and knew it wasn't worth it. Deepest anyone has gone is thirteen. One man. A human, from another human world. Dead within half an hour.

beats.headline: Not until floor twelve
beats.text: Now I'm their registered guide. Walk into any other training guild and it brings them back to this room; they lose me at the fourth floor. At the door I take the kid by the jacket, because this part matters. It's not worth it, no matter what they tell you. Not until floor 12, and even then, negotiate as much as you can. Remember that. Then I shut the door.

beats.headline: Bosses, explained with a hangover
beats.text: They wake me up. The photograph of my brother's on the cot with me, and the bottles are on the floor. Six main kinds of boss, kid: Neighborhood, Borough, City, Province, Country, Floor. And elites, which are not your problem yet. The kid asks if they'll all be people from his world. No, not always. There's a lot of recycling from earlier iterations of the game. Some will be human stock. Most won't be, or they will be and it won't be as obvious. You can't run from most boss fights on the early floors. Be careful.

beats.headline: There will always be clues
beats.text: I read the fight notes. The weight did what his fist would have: the bare knuckle skill is as good as any unenchanted weapon. Give scrolls to the highest intelligence; his fog lasted fifteen seconds, the cat's would have run two minutes. Her potion cooldown is her constitution, and her shred attack is useless until her health catches up. The borough boss? If I knew, I could not say. That is cheating. But the llama died at the throat and the Juicer at the vein. Look for the weakness. There will always be clues. Look for them.

beats.headline: Just those who pay for the privilege
beats.text: The kid gets a war gauntlet with a warning about striking a war god's worshippers, and asks how to spot them. Horses, centaurs, tikbalangs, blue face paint, a lot of talk about wenches and dying gloriously. Then I tell him the part I probably should not. That god isn't real. There are no real gods in this game. He has been saying some of these bosses are like him, down here against their will. Not always, I tell him. Especially further down. There are no gods here. Just those who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: He has done this before, and it cost him everything
beats.text: I crawled. I took Changeling, and I can't shift on my own any more, so the dungeon hands me a body at the start of every floor and I wear what I'm given. This one is a rat-kin. What I actually am is golden, and has wings. I don't talk about the family. When I've had enough to drink, I talk about the family.

beats.headline: A Bugaboo, and a hard no
beats.text: New floor, new body. A Bugaboo this time: seven feet, no neck, and the chairs are too small now. The kid tells me Odette wants me to seek her out. I'd rather spend another two thousand years in this room. Her show, though, you should go on; it's one of the few I'd recommend. And listen. Viewers can see you in here. They can't see me or hear me. Only those with press credentials can. Like Odette.

beats.headline: The Party, in a whisper
beats.text: While the fish and the cat talk Gossip Girl, I get the kid alone. Listen. The Party is the Bloom: ultra-nationalists, under fifteen percent of the vote when I signed my indenture, and now they run the whole kua-tin government. They've run it into the ground. Borant is being forced by its own government to end this game fast; it gets no money until the season's over. The committee has already warned them about the bugs. So the government is working extra hard to get you killed. Don't upset them.

beats.headline: Arcanist, and a brother
beats.text: Now I'm allowed to talk about the third floor, and I've cleaned the place up. Down the stairs, back in this room: race, then class, then stats. The AI will recommend, and its recommendations are good, and they don't care how you look on camera. Me? Arcanist. Changeling Fire Mage Arcanist. I almost picked a class called Storm Commander. Odette talked me out of it. My brother picked it instead, on her recommendation. The third floor itself we'll do when you get there.

beats.headline: Manoeuvred into managing a cat
beats.text: Odette says my memory is the most valuable thing a crawler could get hold of, so the two of them arrange for me to become the cat's manager during class selection, and they make it look like an accident. It was not an accident. I will forgive Donut. Carl, no.

beats.headline: An incubus, in a tuxedo
beats.text: Three hours I have been standing in this tuxedo waiting for them. The third floor has made me an incubus: grey skin, short horns, bat wings, a barbed tail, and a deeper voice. Guildmaster of this guildhall, the tooltip says. Carl tells me I look good. The cat says something about crackers. I welcome them properly, because the training levels are over. Then the door closes, the public cannot see in here, and the jacket and tie come off. I hate formal wear.

beats.headline: Money, and lots of it
beats.text: Compensated Anarchist is potentially the best of the three, and it requires a lot of work: grind, grind, and focus, on shortened timers. He picks it while I narrow my eyes at him. Only one thing is going to make this work, and it is not training. It is money, and lots of it. As a manager I cannot fight beside them, but I can still step outside now and then, especially on the urban levels, and I have to present them. So the tie goes back on.

beats.headline: Props who do not know it
beats.text: Most of the people in these villages were engineered by Borant, so Borant owns them. It is the only world they have known. Every time they are regenerated their minds are altered and planted with false memories, and anything inconvenient, like a crawler explaining that they are props, is erased. Those meth-addicted goblins were written for this world only. Carl asks how that is legal. You cannot alter the memories of naturals unless they sign their rights away. Using the printed ones outside sanctioned entertainment is basically a war crime.

beats.headline: He remembers none of it
beats.text: I am in my room, it is getting late, and Carl asks how my head is. The cat informs me, in capitals, that I molested someone's grandma. I let Carl explain everything, and then I tell them to back out of there and get to the safe room before dark, and that I will explain how stupid they are once they arrive. Then horns and a charm: break your own finger. Then the cat says it is no succubus but an elite. Get out of there. Do not get involved.

beats.headline: An incubus's weakness
beats.text: I apologize. I have not had a drink in an Over City pub in a very long time, and I did not take into account the incubus's weakness, which is alcohol. Sober, I would have told them that quests are great for experience and loot only when you are comfortably ahead of the curve, and with eight days and the two of them playing catch-up, skip it. And once I was cogent, I told them to stay away from the elite. They made a date with her for tomorrow night.

beats.headline: Never trust an elite
beats.text: Elites are never naturals. They are designed, printed and imprinted with the memories their drama needs, and they move freely between the urban floors. This circus is a storyline with its own show and a team of writers, and if the story drifts they hot patch new instructions right into the elite's head. The fairness rules are looser around them. One crawler's life against a drama that has been building for weeks: you know what happens. You are the red shirt. When this floor collapses, the important ones go down to the sixth. Forget the quest. Go to the city.

beats.headline: The rules he cannot break
beats.text: Most of what I know I'm not allowed to volunteer. Some of it I can only give you if you ask the exact question. Without press credentials nobody watching can see me or hear me, and as a manager I can't touch a mob. My advice is what it has always been: stay ahead of the curve, never trust an elite, stay away from gods. Carl has heard all three.

beats.headline: Managers have one rule
beats.text: The Bopca tells me he has not felt himself since those two arrived, so I mix him a draft from behind his own bar. It knocks him out, and I go into his kitchen for the newsletter; shopkeepers get a printed brief after each recap. I take a few herbs while I am there and pass them to Carl under the table. Managers have one rule: no direct battle with mobs. Everything else is fair game. The brief warns of a major battle event in this area today or tonight. Eat, and get to that town.

beats.headline: The cure is not in this town
beats.text: I visit my old friend Eklund, the only game guide in this town I know. He is too smart for his own good and will not look up the Water Lily cure, but he does tell me the name of Signet's programme, and Carl's hunch is correct. Then I have the recipe: Satch Toad extract mixed with a standard healing potion. It negates all naiad sleep effects and curses. Simple. I can buy it at the alchemical market in a medium or large town. Not in this one.

beats.headline: How to kill a Pestiferous Vine
beats.text: I explained it after the recap. A Pestiferous Vine is a trope, lazy writing. Really a fungus hybrid: its spores infect parasitic worms, and the worms infect the mobs. Plants are easy to kill if you know the trick, and this one's trick is poisoned blood. A few drops on the vine break its link with every symbiont, in fifteen to twenty minutes, and it will not know. If it suspects, the same blood with an antidote in it cures it, so it will try to get its monsters to bleed you. A city boss as well? The core should be the same size. I think.

beats.headline: A potion that works on a pet
beats.text: A Heal scroll does nothing for the dinosaur and neither does a potion. Listen. Take out a heal potion. There is a cinnamon stick in your inventory and I gave you a couple of branches of thistle rot. The whole cinnamon stick goes into the potion. Wait five seconds. Add the thistle rot. Cork it, shake it, pour it down the pet's throat, and try not to get your hand bitten off. The cinnamon and the thistle both came out of the Belly Rubbed Pug's kitchens, where I stole them.

beats.headline: The manager goes where Donut goes
beats.text: I pop into my own room with a drink in my hand, because nobody warned me. As a manager, my town now matches wherever Donut last entered; a plain guide can dial it anywhere. There is a guide-only town these two cannot reach, and I was looking forward to it. The drink works because I brewed a potion that lets alcohol affect demon spawn. On my world I was a mycologist. Odette made me learn plenty about vegetation when we made it to the sixth floor. The cat gives Carl a sharp look when I say that. Neither of them says anything.

beats.headline: You can't save them all
beats.text: An orc woman at the pub, GumGum, says she needs our help. No. Not tonight. It is a quest, and we are doing no more quests on this floor. Then the kid wanders back out of his room, and she is already gone. So I tell him, and I want it to sink into that thick skull. You can't save them all. The people running this know who you are, and they will always be baiting you. If you truly want to help others, get as strong and as deep as possible.

beats.headline: Immortal, sort of
beats.text: Carl asks why I was so upset to be picked. It is not you. It's complicated. Then he asks whether that opossum was right that I am immortal. Sort of. From the fourth floor, managers get a protection package. Not you. We can still be hurt and still feel it, but dying there only kicks us out of the game. For the rest of this floor I am as unprotected as you. If I die as a manager I am done for the season. The rules pay me more the longer Donut survives, and past the ninth it is an obscene amount. Let's go look at the Silk Road.

beats.headline: City elves and a squiggly letter
beats.text: The shirt is from the 201st Security Group, the city elves' militia. Conspiracy nuts, too stupid for the high elves, who kick them out. Their cause is protecting the eagle folk, my own old people, whom they take for angels, all because of a few stories about their tree goddess. I have never known them to be violent. The cat declares she is doing the quest; I ain't your dad, I'm your manager. Then the letter off the dead orc. I can't read it, but I know these squiggles. Necroscript. You two might have a lich problem.

beats.headline: New rule: nothing outside the dungeon
beats.text: I distinctly remember saying subtle. The kid calls an orc king a pussy on air, the king's son lasers the wrong trailer from orbit, and the Valtay answer by blowing up the royal yacht. His wife is dead. So, new rule. We do not mention anyone outside this dungeon, not until after the sixth floor, if these two idiots make it that far. Odette asks, they have no opinion. I wanted his people aimed at the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor. I don't think that's going to be an issue now. What can he do to them in here? Nothing yet. That changes very soon.

beats.headline: What the newsletter does not say
beats.text: I talk Fitz into showing me his herb stash and steal his newsletter. Borant is warning shopkeepers and pub owners to be extra careful not to anger crawlers. It doesn't say why. I can read between the lines. Some of you are getting stronger than you should; the kid who trashed the Desperado Club is proof. Borant controls the mobs and most of the experience. The System AI controls most of the loot boxes, it is still the ultimate arbiter, and it is evening the odds against the shorter floors. These elaborate quests are the same symptom. Keep the new girl alive. If she dies, get those rings off her.

beats.headline: Liches never shut up
beats.text: Liches come in all shapes and power levels. But they all have one thing in common. They are just like Odette: they never, ever shut the hell up. Narcissists, and cowards, who will do anything not to let go of the life they have grabbed back, so they always have minions and grandiose plans. I said blow the building and take a chance on losing the quest. Then they killed most of his support, and I changed my mind: he'll be weak. One more wrinkle. The last one was a neighbourhood boss. I'd bet my left nipple this is a borough boss. Come prepared.

beats.headline: A bereft minion, then run
beats.text: Not a lich, he says. No. A bereft minion: one still alive after its controller is dead. You killed the head bad guy when you blew up Miss Quill. Quests sometimes look bigger than they are; I should have known, it was only a silver quest. Sorry about the dynamite. Get the story, put him down, get out before the swordsmen wake. Then the quest drops. Run for the Desperado Club; the second room is out of the blast. Protective Shell won't work, it's magical. Break the gem? Probably makes it blow early. It's called The Fools Who Broke the Glass for a reason.

beats.headline: The skill that stayed behind
beats.text: Kid, listen. Her Negotiation came at level five with the Artist Alley class, and she sold it up to seven. The class is gone and the five levels went with it, but she kept the two she earned, experience and all, so it bumped itself to four. So a skill she levels even once, she keeps. Stat points, no. Use Mongo as much as you can and Mascot stays. Watch for classes with rare spells. And it's probably a bug, so don't talk about it out loud. They won't notice until she carries a spell down a floor.

beats.headline: A toad, not a frog
beats.text: This floor they've made me Grulke Infantry. Toad warriors: leapers, a tongue that hits hard, and a people gone to mercenaries and vagrants. Tunnel trolls hunt them to lick them. Don't ever call a real Grulke a frog; they're mean bastards. Toads. And yes, I know about the quest. I get notices of court decisions that go against my client. You got screwed, but you're alive. The third floor is usually twenty days, and you had ten. Level 27 and 26 after that is lucky and a miracle. We can't rely on luck.

beats.headline: Two hours of sleep, then a schedule
beats.text: You only sleep two hours now, so I'll see you out here for the recap. Then the schedule. Wake, eat, buffs: shower, the cat's brushing, your feet. An hour in the training room on one skill, because you only get one a day. Carl, Smush. Katia, Catcher. Donut picked Dodge. Crafting after that, starting tomorrow. The recap freezes on REDACTED; get used to it, that's the part explaining the level. Where I woke up was station 317: the Yellow and Emerald lines, and a big one called the Misery. I wrote it all down.

beats.headline: A control sigil
beats.text: That's a control sigil. Only you can see it, because of your Escape Plan skill. Secondary programs like Vengeance of the Daughter use them, and so do the dungeon's makers sometimes, though it's considered sloppy programming because they're easy to break. They're mostly for controlled gating: stopping a specific type of mob passing. The showrunners turn them on and off, not the AI, which is why they use them. Blue means it's on. It'll have no effect on you. Can crawlers make one? No. There's a similar kind of magic you'll never have the mana for. Donut might.

beats.headline: Special Brew and potion balls
beats.text: Get back. You'll contaminate it. I put Donut's two table upgrades into the alchemy table, so it's level three. Two of my Special Brew: thirty seconds of healing and regeneration, near enough immortality, but not against decapitation or blowing yourself up. It adds about ten hours to your potion sickness, and two is the lifetime limit; I've never got past that. Two Superb Constitution potions for the cat. And fragmenting potion balls: pour a potion in, throw it at a bad guy. Potions work on mobs. It doesn't make sense. It's always been that way.

beats.headline: Naughty, for seven days
beats.text: The Prize Carousel materialises in the personal space, and its host is Chaco the Bard. Guide Mordecai throws a metal chair at him with his tongue. The chair stops a quarter of an inch from the host's head. Naughty. Mordecai blinks out, and the room marked Manager goes with him. Time out: seven days, for violating the rules, which returns him with a day and a half left on the floor. Chaco says it was a long time ago, that he was doing what Mordecai's manager told him, and asks that Mordecai be told he is sorry.

beats.headline: Seven days, in a blink
beats.text: Where is he? Where did that — oh. By his left tit. The notifications say seven days. For me no time has passed at all; I lost my temper at Chaco, blinked, and here I am. The cat has a player-killer skull over her head. So does Katia. The dinosaur is jumping circles around me. I see I have missed a few things. Carl starts to tell me, and then Katia erupts. Blood, gallons of it, in every direction, over the walls and the ceiling and me, and I go backward over the couch with my legs in the air.

beats.headline: The map is the Syndicate logo
beats.text: Look at the named lines from above: rings of different sizes, overlapping. That's the Syndicate logo, and the Nightmare's loop is the second ring. So a train has to loop to the front, and you already found it: the Escape Velocity line, named for the ship that found the wormhole that led to the Vog Generation Ship. The abyss is the centre of the galaxy; the tracks are the original worm paths. Six station mimics are the H'lene, who set six waystations near the centre as traps and ate the travellers. The Valtay and the orcs wiped them out. They really went all out.

beats.headline: No cooldown on a god
beats.text: Carl, if you've summoned Grull: run. Don't fight him. He's invulnerable. Take my special brew. You haven't? By the gods, don't scare me like that. The rules, then. An involuntary summoning lasts the vessel's level in seconds plus the god's. Grull is sanctum tier, level 250; from a level-forty vessel that's 290 seconds. Summoned, he grows until he fills the room. There's no cooldown, and a god held in one summoning breaks out and goes to the next if someone calls him. I learned that the hard way. The hardest way possible. Now don't you even dare think about —

beats.headline: Fifteen days is a warning
beats.text: I was expecting twelve days. They gave us fifteen, and three extra days are not a gift, they're a nasty surprise waiting to happen. I got here first and gathered what I could: two towns, a sandstorm an hour or two a day, a castle that's a speck against the top of the dome, and maybe three dozen crawlers in this quadrant, every one I've seen so underpowered it's a miracle they're alive. Then the announcement. Four quadrants, four castles, and the stairwell won't open until all four fall. So assume the other hundred and fifty are idiots. Eat. Open your boxes. Sleep.

beats.headline: Pawna's Tears, saved
beats.text: Every box on this floor is handing out water-breathing scrolls and antidotes. That's the floor telling you what's coming, kid. Then Carl opens his deity box and I have to ask to hold it. Pawna's Tears. Goddess of peace, Grull's sister and enemy. Plus five to any skill he picks, and unlike a Cheat Code it doesn't have to be drunk on the spot. Train something to fifteen, take it, and it's twenty. Single best piece of loot he's had since he came in. Not including the pet biscuit, the cat says. Fine. We decide after he picks his subclass.

beats.headline: Selling to the armies
beats.text: The marketplace interface is on Donut's account, because her Charisma goes into the prices. For now it's a virtual general store. Once the sixth floor opens, the tourists and the factions trade through it too, and anything magical you list gets snapped up, because this is how they outfit their armies. Yes, kid, you might be selling to people you'll fight. If you don't sell your gear, somebody else will, and they'll mostly be using it on each other. Once the ninth floor opens the factions can't buy new gear at all. I'll explain that when you get there.

beats.headline: Safe only with a crawler inside
beats.text: Kid, a saferoom protects whoever's in it, but a Borant-owned NPC alone in one isn't protected. If there are no crawlers or off-world NPCs in the room, the room's probably gone with the rest. The Toe isn't a real saferoom; if the proprietor isn't a Bopca, it's about fifty-fifty. Our personal space is. So if the gnomes do to this town what they just did to the Bactrian one, you come in here. There are other rules, and the manual on saferoom procedures is like a phonebook. The primary and secondary zones are different; they don't directly touch crawlers or NPCs at all.

beats.headline: Rapid Detox, and a wasted spell
beats.text: One of these two fuckwits has his boots on the table, so I land on it, and it breaks, and I tell them to shut up for five minutes while I brew. Rapid Detox, with sage beetle ichor so they can't read the label. Clears alcohol and most drugs, and for one floor, if they drink, they get violently ill. The good kind of poisoning. Then the part that matters: Louis carries an enhanced, legendary-tier Cloud of Exhaust, almost certainly the same spell the goat lady has, and he's been using it to run away. He should be level forty by now.

beats.headline: A sect after a full library
beats.text: Ah, shit. I should have known. Changeling Principals. It's an old story; I haven't seen it used in a long, long time. They're a sect of changeling culture, cultish, like those city elves, but less apocalyptic and more power hungry. They're obsessed with a full library, and since a changeling can only become something it has physically touched, they go after rare creatures. Get the brain, kid, the glowing part. If you kill one, take the head; I can make a potion from it. Only if it's untransformed when it dies. Knock them out first.

beats.headline: A timeout, not a glitch
beats.text: I felt it. It happens. That half-second freeze usually isn't a glitch; it's a gameplay timeout, so the dueling routines can reconcile a rule conflict. An artifact is a legendary or celestial-tier item you find lying around or drop as loot, and they start turning up around the eighth or ninth floor. The showrunners control the storylines, but the AI picks the specific loot, and it can and will adjust the story to keep the game fair. If you get what I'm saying. And remember what I said about the word feral.

beats.headline: This is not a daycare
beats.text: I don't have the materials for Feather Fall; the seed pods are scarce until the sixth floor. I can make him one kind of potion, two doses, and he won't like it. Then he walks in with forty children. This isn't a goddamned daycare, Carl. Do you see a jungle gym? So I stream a movie to the screen from the library I collected before we went live. Toy Story. It's a manager benefit, for strategizing on the screens. Now the cat knows. And that is why I never told her.

beats.headline: Sell the kit, use the stone
beats.text: Kid, keep the Half Splat in your hotlist until you find a real Featherfall; it stops the fall killing you and leaves you at five percent. And don't knock Dolores Doesn't Splat. Unpleasant, sure, but you landed at a hundred percent. The platinum stone is what I was talking about: items that enhance the items you already have. Use it now, it has a short shelf life. The author kit you'll never have the skills for; a simple Light scroll would take a week of practice. Sell it. One guy last season used the same scroll over two hundred times and learned the spell.

beats.headline: Infiltrators
beats.text: Oh, fuck. Shoot him again. I've told you about brain worms, kid. Intellect hunters take corpses, and the bodies rot. The Valtay keep their bodies alive. Their cousins, the Scree, are better known as the Infiltrators: they take living bodies, and after a few days the host is locked out and watches himself move like a puppet. She's in his brain. His body is her armor. Getting her out without killing him? Next to impossible. There's an antiparasitic that will kill her, and I won't have the materials until the next floor.

beats.headline: Veriluxx, and who owns it
beats.text: Kid, don't press your luck with that panel. It's a non-enhanced toy; set off the self-destruct and I honestly don't know what the AI does with it. Most toys need a licensed enhancement zone, and some need a license key in the kid to prove his parents paid their taxes. This one needs neither. As for Veriluxx: never heard of them, but the logo says Veritan Linkage, a mostly-Soother lending fund that advocates enslaving people who can't pay their taxes. Odds are it's a way to funnel money to Borant. Carl asks if the whole universe is assholes. Just the ones with the money.

beats.headline: A liaison hold
beats.text: I didn't think I'd see you again, kid. I got a notice there was a liaison hold on Donut, and then five days were gone. Only the fifth floor, and the liaisons are already involved. By his left tit. Next thing you know, the lawyers will be here, and everything gets complicated once the lawyers get here. A Syndicate liaison, and he let you walk right out? Then the kid pulls Loita's rebreather out of his waistband. He looted it off her body.

beats.headline: Do not let it touch you
beats.text: Do not let it touch you. Once a sand ooze gets ahold of you it's like quicksand, and Carl's already burned his Protective Shell. It won't just suffocate you, kid. It pours sand into every opening you've got until you burst, and he's wearing boxers. They hunt by vibration and sound, not heat, so clomping across a ceiling will still get noticed; he'll need one of the toys he was building. And I wouldn't trust a guy who married an ooze. Katia, watch him while Carl's in there.

beats.headline: Two potions he should not drink
beats.text: Carl's Pacifist box gives him two Potions of Bloodlust. Double strength, double speed, half dexterity, half constitution, and a debuff that means you don't remember where you are or why you're fighting. Don't use those. The last time I saw someone drink that potion, they accidentally killed half of their party. And don't get ideas about the gate either, kid. Crawlers can't hop floors. If you ever get the last watch, stick it in your inventory until you're strong enough to deal with whatever comes out. Which will be never.

beats.headline: Keep her, as a trainer
beats.text: A withering spirit. Sometimes a soul gets split, and the two halves try to reunite in a proper vessel; when that goes wrong, you get this. Not alive, not dead, hard to kill, mostly harmless, haunting the object. They use them as quest-givers a lot. We avoid gods like we avoid outside factions. And then, knowing I'll regret it, I say we keep her. In the saferoom she can't summon anything, and a minor deity may know potions. Donut can hire her as a trainer. She'll live in a corner of the training room.

beats.headline: Drakea was a bune
beats.text: I remember Drakea. A bune: a slight, dragon-like people, peaceful by nature, some of the cleverest fighters there are. Class like Carl's, but more magic. A big trap guy. He died on the eleventh floor. Or was it the twelfth? He'd had a pretty good offer and spat in their faces, and then his setup backfired. Unnaturally backfired. Lawyers got involved, and the Syndicate, acting on his behalf, collected a big sum from the Sultanate.

beats.headline: Going primal
beats.text: The AI handing out stock and pictures of plaintiffs' mothers is worrisome. It's supposed to help monitor prohibited speech against the sponsors, not go all in and participate. That usually happens, but at the end, when the system has gone bonkers around the twelfth floor. All large-scale AIs go insane, given time; there's even a term for it, Primal Degeneration. And no, kid, nobody takes it out behind the woodshed. A Macro AI is a lifeform, protected by Syndicate law. It gets its own sealed system to bounce around in for the rest of eternity.

beats.headline: A shrine in the saferoom
beats.text: A shrine has just appeared in the saferoom. A sun disk, a cup and a skull. It does not say which god, but I am guessing Emberus, and I want to know which of these two idiots is responsible. The cat says it was Carl. Of course it was. I call him an idiot and leave it there, because there is real work: with Samantha's help I have figured out the yam. Each potion takes about an eighth of it. One is ready for him, the second is on the table, and he wants three.

beats.headline: Their schedule, not yours
beats.text: Carl expected a patch to stop the gate trick. They did the opposite, and I am not surprised. They love it when you do stupid, suicidal things, but when it involves the entire population, they start to get alarmed. Don't mistake that for kindness. Once all the sponsorships are done, don't expect them to cushion your fall. Meanwhile the personal space is a wreck, the kids are watching The Goonies, and the changelings are dancing like portly little humans with their shirts pulled up.

beats.headline: Toss the ring
beats.text: A platinum emergency box. Do you know what that cost? More than the GDP of some star systems. Forget it and go down the stairs. Then he carries the doll's head outside, where she will summon a god, and she does. Then Larracos. Carl. Son. You don't know the forces you're dealing with. You got this far because you make them a lot of money, and you just kicked them in the financial balls. I don't care what that ring is worth. Toss it before the stairs. You can't fight a war like this and expect to win.

beats.headline: A Pocket Kuma
beats.text: You had to go and challenge all the hunters, and now look. And that doesn't look like a melee class to me. Laugh it up, Carl. Get it out of your system. This floor I'm a Pocket Kuma: knee-high, buck teeth, elf ears, a monkey tail and eyes like a baby's. Half-fairy, bred as a pet for the High Elf court, until King Finian learned they were intelligent and had them executed. They can't fight and they can barely walk. I jump for my doorknob, hang off it, and the door opens on its own.

beats.headline: That was an accident
beats.text: The cleric bear, Tam, is shouting down at me that the naiad and dinosaur rules have to come back. I ask him why it's necessary. The guards will keep the town safe regardless. Have there been naiad attacks recently? Always, he says, and the lizards are worse, and if the pagan monkey won't restore the rules, you'll have to go out there and do something about the dinosaur menace. Ah, hell. Sorry, guys. That was an accident. And no, I don't know what the town upgrade is. Everything on my manager menu has moved around.

beats.headline: Reading the shop software
beats.text: The kid says they told him my contract's still being honored. We'll see. This sort of thing happens a lot, just not usually mid-season: contracts frozen, guides traded to other companies, lawyers and rule changes for cycles. I check whether the shop is still running kua-tin software or the Valtay's. It looks the same, which is good and bad. They'll keep the fantasy theme, hopefully. Meanwhile the Ursine finally understand they're in danger, we beat back two more Dream elves, and they've talked Imani into being guildmaster. Katia wants to borrow money for a manager's headquarters, so I keep my room.

beats.headline: He did the con once
beats.text: The kid's fan box is a CrawlCon badge. I haven't seen them use current crawlers for the con in over a century. I was a special guest once, years after my season. All I did was the autograph session, and I only ended up signing three items. Three events means they're going all in. He asks how this is even a thing. The first active prep teams landed on his planet in 1936. The first sci-fi convention was in Philadelphia in 1938. Do the math. And no, Donut. Sorry, kid. This one's just Carl.

beats.headline: Youth assistants shouldn't be here
beats.text: Loop-de-Loop, kid: a trap spell, not a module trap. She can send you somewhere or swap places with you, and she peppers every town she enters with them. Exploits that let one crawler trap and kill another usually don't get patched. Then Donut tells me what the show cut: Lucia named someone invisible, Alexandro, her youth assistant. Children under a certain age are taken out of the dungeon until the crawl is over, and youth assistants look after them. Kids shouldn't be in here. Youth assistants shouldn't be here. It's really strange.

beats.headline: Starting to feel obsolete
beats.text: Every day, kid, you do and come across something that's never been done or seen before. I'm starting to feel a little obsolete. You want to know if you can use that table? Ask your lawyer. If he doesn't respond, wait until after the next recap, and if they don't take it away from you, install it in the crafting studio and start working. In the meantime, transcribe everything you can from that automaton book into your scratchpad. And the stores in Nipton are terrible.

beats.headline: He testified against Odette
beats.text: I'd like to see that one go to trial. Odette's was a farce, a whole production, and she pleaded down to a lesser charge just before they reached a verdict. Yes, kid, I saw it. I testified in it. Against her. She wasn't charged when she was a crawler, which was long before me. It was when she was my manager. Now open your boxes and get back out there.

beats.headline: Fifty cycles chasing a recipe
beats.text: The Apothecary's silver box is a potion recipe and a drawing of Mongo. Holy cow. I've been chasing this one for fifty cycles. You don't chill it: you put it in the centrifuge and flash-freeze it. Of course. So simple. Charm Animal, brewed for one animal, and the special ingredient is a liter of that animal's blood, per potion. We've got the thorn sap tips. We've got the last ingredient too, and he's hiding behind Donut. I'll make him a sleeping potion, Donut. He won't even know.

beats.headline: Let her die, he says
beats.text: Or you let her die and collect her gear in the morning. Two sponsors who know more than you do just spent a fortune protecting you from vampirism, and a vampire asks for help the moment the sun sets. I know I'm not as valuable as I once was, kid, but I can see a connection. He's going anyway. So take these. Holy Goopers: shrine water, a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant in a potion ball. Emberus is a light god. To a vampire it's napalm.

beats.headline: Stay away from the creepers
beats.text: Listen to me. I think I've seen this on a smaller scale. Those glamoured fragments were going to become Glamoured Creepers, and with their boss cured something else has taken them over, probably an Odious Blossom. They rip parts off people and grow stronger. Poison darts. Up out of the ground. Something that big needs an aerosol, and delivery is the problem. The prize is too good, which means it's too dangerous. For the sake of the gods, stay away from them.

beats.headline: Uncle Morty's Insta Lawn-Kill
beats.text: He swallowed it whole? You're all crazy. It'll make its way out again. Four jugs on the counter: Uncle Morty's Insta Lawn-Kill and Undead Repellant, Extra-Strength Edition. I took a weedkiller built for an odious bloom and stacked anti-undead boosts on it, like the holy grenade I made the kid. Two or three creepers a jug. Do not get close. Apply it at maximum distance. It's flammable, and if it burns before it soaks in, it won't work. Nobody listens to Mordecai anymore, do they?

beats.headline: Notes are paid by the character
beats.text: Notes are expensive. You pay by the character and the rules are complicated, so they force you into code; be too clear and the AI translates it for you, and you don't want that. Then I watch the kid hand the cat a plus-three potion from his own sponsor box, telling her it's so she can top off Magic Missile, and I don't buy it. I open my mouth. He gives me the smallest shake of his head. Fine. I move off.

beats.headline: Not like the Naga season
beats.text: The hunters are dying in numbers nobody has ever seen. And this isn't like the Naga season, where they bled money with every bad decision. It started that way. Now it's the opposite: everyone else is losing money, and all of it is flowing into Borant. Too bad for the kua-tin government that they couldn't keep their little flippers on the company. No offense, Zev, if you're listening. She is.

beats.headline: If it goes sour
beats.text: Five sponsor items from the same outfit, each sent to a different crawler, every one of them with a note to give it to the cat. I've never seen anything like this. Enchanted and nothing more, some of them; you can enchant an item with no properties so it works on ghosts. The kid says he doesn't like all these loose ends, that something is going to go wrong. It always does. If it goes sour, you have the escape plan. Get to the Twister and fly away.

beats.headline: Forget everything else. Get that.
beats.text: If that fuck tit Chaco is in the room with you, kid, a dynamite stick would be a personal favour. Now read me the counter. The potions are a waste; Donut takes ten percent to her lowest base stat and the random spell book. What's a memorial crystal? Forget everything else. Get that. Soul crystals come out of Scolopendra's lair. Memorial crystals come from fallen gods and demigods, full of god-tier spells and knowledge, and you charge one by wearing it and killing things. A hundred hands. He has sixty-six.

beats.headline: Huanxin, Uzzi, and what happened
beats.text: Chaco. Uzzi. A stairwell on the tenth floor that would not open until a god's spell hit the puzzle, and me volunteering to take the hit, because the only life it cost was mine. Odette found a cheaper way to pay. Huanxin Jinx was driving the storm goddess, and when she raised her price from a tenth of Odette's bonus to a third, Odette refused. She talked Chaco into putting the dart into my brother instead. The goddess died in the containment and the stairwell opened. I went through it. He did not.

beats.headline: Hills Cyclops, and a warning
beats.text: Hills Cyclops. Level fifty, pink, one eye, and the description has opinions about sheep. It still beats the ten minutes the seventh floor was open, when I was a slime with no arms. Now, the problem. Samantha flew back here and pushed through the brambles to the door. Withering spirits should not be able to do any of that. I don't understand it, which makes it extra dangerous. She won't shut up about the flesh golem in Carl's inventory. Kid, don't give it to her until we figure out why and how she is gaining this power.

beats.headline: Drain it every time
beats.text: Divine items are the best items, kid, whatever the debuffs. And yes, there is somebody in my room. With the upgraded quarters I was able to hire a room attendant. It's not important. Concentrate on your sewing; you can ruin the item. Then Soul Reaper comes up. Oh, it's good. It's also more dangerous than Donut's berserking spell. Drain the essence bar each time it fills, and don't store the stuff for long. I once saw a crawler fill her reserve with gorgons and kill a country boss with a single attack. It turned to stone and shattered.

beats.headline: Do whatever she tells you
beats.text: Carl messages from the door of Club Vanquisher. A goddess called Eileithyia has given them a quest, she is being driven by Huanxin Jinx, and would I tell him everything I know. I take a while answering that. Do whatever she tells you to do. The rest I'll say face to face, not in chat. Katia and Bautista are here already, and Katia has caught me up on a little of it. Nobody decides anything until he gets back.

beats.headline: The last time someone refused her
beats.text: Katia wants the attendant boon. It's usually a cushy gig, and hurting an attendant brings a world of pain down on you. It still happens, especially once the games begin. The Maestro will have access to her, and so will sponsors whose friends may have taken a financial kicking when she flooded Larracos. A viper den. Then Carl asks about Huanxin. Rich, very intelligent, a brat when she was younger, has played the Ascendency since she was a kid and never won, suspended once for bribery. We're not getting into it. She can go fuck herself. So why tell him to obey her? Because the last time someone didn't, my brother died.

beats.headline: Six attendants, on the supply money
beats.text: They walk in early, and I still have a pink bow on my head and lipstick across my face. Cyclops. No depth perception, and I can't see my own reflection. Donut offers application tips. Carl spots the split controller on the floor and works it out. I'm allowed an attendant, and I took the slot, then filled their five too: Ruby and the others with compression sickness, who I didn't think would survive the fight at the end of the last floor. A little over a thousand gold a day, out of the supply money. Carl says he'd have said yes. I stand by my decision.

beats.headline: Liquid Therapy, for the whole guild
beats.text: The spider has Unending Insanity and Lights Out, both level fifteen, and neither one comes off without a god. So I brew Liquid Therapy. One dose a day, good until you sleep, covers both of those and most of the fear effects besides. The ingredients are not cheap and I am making enough for the whole guild. Carl spent both his table upgrade coupons on my alchemy table to make it happen. Mongo's dose is not ready yet.

beats.headline: Her or Donut
beats.text: Four drugs. Travis Priest, Creamsicle Charm, the blitz, and Glory Bound, once, thank goodness, and that one's cure is a bad trip on purpose: she relives one of her worst memories. Then I say the part I can't say to Donut. Son, I know you love Katia. I also know you love Donut more. The right thing is to help her. The smart, safe thing is to step back and let her self-destruct, because it is her or Donut. Some breaks aren't clean. He tells me not to bring it up again.

beats.headline: Vorpal is a condition
beats.text: Vorpal is a condition, not a species. Feral means touched by the Nothing; vorpal means deputised by the gods. Celestial guards, foot soldiers, suicide bombers, any race at all. The nearer a demon, the stronger and angrier they get, and they drag its aggro onto themselves. Losing a fight, they explode and take the room with them. Stay the hell away. And Li Na is a demon race, so if they smell her, they follow her upstairs. Get out and let security deal with it.

beats.headline: How to kill a hydra
beats.text: Holy shit. Okay, kid, listen. Each head gives the whole thing a different resistance, and its attack mirrors that resistance. Magic won't do much. Physical attacks or your explosions, necks and heads only; the body is practically indestructible. Cut a head off and it grows right back. So find the one resistant to fire, cut it off, and cauterize the wound before it returns. Then you can burn the whole. Blowing a head stops its resistance until it regrows, but you need a nice flat cut to keep it down. Now's the time for that wand you bought from Chaco.

beats.headline: Eye in the Sky, level ten
beats.text: That's a really powerful spell, and it was probably a scroll. I've seen them maybe once or twice. Like Find Crawler, but it covers the whole area. They come in five, ten and fifteen. At fifteen you'd get no warning. At five you'd learn who cast it. That was a ten. Whoever it was now knows where you are and what level you are. So keep moving.

beats.headline: Early, and it belongs to the ninth
beats.text: Holy shit. Okay, pay attention. This normally happens at the end of the ninth floor, when there are two or three teams left; it's setup for the Ascendency fight. It resets when you go down the stairs, but it'll pop off earlier on every floor down from here. Chop the heads off what you kill. Stay away from weak undead. If a demon grabs you, a portal opens and you're both dragged to Sheol. Automatic death. If you want to save Imani, reach that nun first.

beats.headline: Self-preservation is not selfish
beats.text: You need to quit trying to help everybody else and save your own ass. Both halves of a two-part trap have to be set by the same crawler. And you want to pull a bone out of yourself to save another crawler, and lose the jacket and every benefit on it, for a key trick I've never even heard of. Magic keys don't always work as advertised. Everybody else needs you. Donut needs you. Self-preservation is not selfishness.

beats.headline: The short version of Sheol
beats.text: Short version, because you asked for short. It was set up a long time ago and nobody has ever gotten that far, so it has been running on its own for seasons. The demons get pulled out for quests and fights, but nobody sees Sheol itself. No tourists. There is a queen, and four sons, the princes, near enough gods, and you are looking at one of them. The princes shared a harem until one brother banished the lot to the Nothing. Under them, a matriarchal culture we hear about and never see. That guy shouldn't be here this early.

beats.headline: What the Nebulars actually want
beats.text: Ysalte? Then listen. She has been getting sponsored recently, by the Nebular team. The same ones sponsoring your nun. Near the centre of the galaxy there's a big AI, same sort of thing that runs the crawl but older than the Syndicate, stable, no personality. The Nebs worship it and think copying it is blasphemy. They want to shut the crawl down, and they keep trying to win the Celestial Ascendency, because a prize is a seat on the crawl council. Don't get excited. They preach wiping out every planet that could host a crawl, and everyone on it. Pacifists, outside the dungeon. Psychotic.

beats.headline: A Canadian, with a better table
beats.text: I walk out of the crafting room in a snowsuit and a raccoon hat, and the two of them laugh at me. I don't pick the clothes. Human this time, Canadian, glasses. The table is upgraded higher than I have ever had it, and for the first time I can examine a potion and see how it was made. So, listen. Nobody reads a spellbook until we talk. Quan's cloak needs a plan before Donut puts it on. And the ceasefire can end early three ways. All unlikely. You never know.

beats.headline: Seriously scary bastards
beats.text: The skill potion comes back from my table, and I was wrong: I can make these. A few more table upgrades and some very specialised ingredients. Drink it now, I tell Carl, and train with whatever it gives you. Gloom Wraith Phase, level 13. So I say it straight. You two have always been powerful for your levels. You are now the most powerful crawlers I have ever worked with, including some who made it through floor 11. Then five minutes on practising, and on not phasing into solid objects.

beats.headline: Summon Ally, explained
beats.text: The kid asks me mid-hearing what Summon Ally does, so I tell him. It's a rare teleport, and it's built so the summoned holds the cards. You have to share a chat, the warlord chat counts, apparently. You have to accept. You can't be dropped into a wall. You went over as a ghost because the system compensates for being out cold. I thought I'd killed you. At best they wanted your treatment ruined. At worst it would simply kill you. They wanted to kill us using that crazy spider.

beats.headline: Not a wake-up salve
beats.text: Out loud, for whoever is listening, I say I'm going to pull him out with a Shock Wake salve, adjusted to work on a non-corporeal form. That's not what I'm making. I know we're being watched from outside, so what I actually brew is something to violently expel the spider from him. Not a wake-up salve at all. It's a risky move. I put it on his see-through chest, and he buckles.

beats.headline: Destroy the bait shop
beats.text: I agree. Destroy the bait shop, and do it now. They can drop a nuke through that door and be done with it: the walls will be okay, but everyone inside the castle turns into mince. They needed the mages out first, and that failed, but they might try it anyway. The only reason they haven't is probably that orc out there wants you himself. And if you only collapse the front, guard it, kid. An enemy splashes a Fix potion on it, or reads an Emergency Repair scroll, and you're back where you started.

beats.headline: Two of the same religion, no more
beats.text: Potion balls lined up on the kitchen table, and Carl sweeping them into his inventory. Be careful, Carl. You're playing with fire. Don't hurt anybody you don't have to. We'll be neck deep in gods in a few days, and every one you piss off now is going to come straight for you. Don't use those on more than two of the same religion. He snaps that he knows how this works. Then he stops, smiles, thanks me, and asks me to thank Tiatha for the capacitor wire. Your plans are always bonkers, Carl. But this one...

beats.headline: Harpocrates hates sound
beats.text: Donut, do NOT use the PA while Harpocrates is out. He's the god of silence, not deaf, and he can hear a fly's heartbeat from half a planet away. He'll come for anyone too loud. Meatus started as a gremlin who stole Harpocrates's dink and sewed it on himself. The gremlin stays small. The dink comes at full god size, it's sapient, it's very loud, and it likes music too much to go back. Harpo will kill Meatus, try to do something with him, fail, and smash anything noisy until he times out.

beats.headline: Anne of Green Gables
beats.text: Ruby's in my lap with her head on my shoulder and I'm reading her Anne of Green Gables. The bot's listening too. Carl bursts in with the shark, the meatball, a slug and two crying women from some other party, and stops, and looks at us like he wants to say something. He doesn't. He dials the Larracos gate on the door, and they go.

beats.headline: Deity spells
beats.text: By his left tit, Donut. By his left tit. Those spells you just got are deity spells. I think you're now the most powerful crawler in the history of this game. You've got choices to make, too, because your strength and intelligence are both over a hundred, and the notification probably won't go away until you pick. She picks Muscle Mommy. Are you sure about that one? Too late, she says. Yeah. I think the Bopcas will be worshipping you again, kid. Your charm and Love Vampire skills are stronger than most gods'.

beats.headline: He is Louis's heart
beats.text: Okay. We've been talking with some former crawlers. Fang got out of the War Crime because he's a tiny bit of biology inside a robot, and true offspring of the Initial have survived catastrophes before. He went for the only teammate he had left, his dragon, and was taking her over when the bomb pulse got her. Laundry Day might have worked on him. We should have tried that. Tagg's still a gosh darn mystery. They were replacing Louis's organs, and once they had the brain he'd take control. Maggie was inside Chris's brain. Tagg isn't in Louis's heart, kid. He is Louis's heart.

beats.headline: Allowed under the non-combatant code
beats.text: Listen. This is a surgical procedure, allowed under the non-combatant code, and the second party is an empty shell. I cut down the centre of Louis's chest. We're rigging about thirty lines to bring Tagg's machinery out in one piece when he stops the heart early. I can't be the one to pull it; that could count as an attack. Someone else yanks it out. Donut pours the Special Brew, the naiad organs go in, I sew the rebreather into the bronchial, cast a Water Breathing scroll and run tubes to the gills. Done, with ten seconds left.

beats.headline: My mother's ashes
beats.text: No, I can't touch you. Not directly. See this? A crossbow bolt. Nothing magical about it. My brother died because of you, and because of Odette, and because of Chaco. But mostly because of you. Some of my mother's ashes are built into the tip. In my culture you make a weapon from the ashes of those you lost. She died before the crawl came to my world, and I'm grateful she gets to avenge her son. Goodbye, Katia. Be safe, kid. I load it into the crossbow on the cat's back and walk out.

beats.headline: I gained more
beats.text: The last minute on the floor, and I'm sitting in the dirt with a cigarette and a bottle of Crown Royal, dawn coming up, red comets streaking off the volcano. Carl says get back in the saferoom. I lost so much today. But I think I gained more. I stand, wipe myself off, and throw the bottle through the rotten roots. Thank you, Donut, for setting that up. Then I step toward the door.

beats.headline: Not a Moon Reaper
beats.text: Kid, listen. I look like a Moon Reaper on this floor, and I'm not one. I'm a shadow mimic. Mimics take the shape; changelings get some of the powers. This form is an impossible combination, which is why I keep glitching into a cat, an otter, a slug. And the prophecy business is a Moon Reaper thing. It only happens once for each of you. Nobody give it any weight. Predictions in here are vague, scary and made to fit whatever happens. And keep Rend out of here. His weakness is Reaper Gaze.

beats.headline: Dipped in radiant light
beats.text: That was a celestial boon. Permanent, and it lives in her body, not in her spell list. Her right front claws cut through anything in the mortal realm, ghosts included, and her Claw skill has gone past the cap to seventeen, because when it comes to gods all bets are off. With that constitution she has gone from a ranged powerhouse to one of the strongest melee fighters the game has seen. Now the warning. The game has ways of compensating for overpowered crawlers on this floor and past it. Believe me. Don't get complacent.

beats.headline: Leave the costume on
beats.text: Kid, listen. How high has the costume skill gone? If it's above level three or so, taking that thing off might take a lot of your skin with it. Above five I wouldn't risk it. Six, he says, with a bunch of other skills hanging off it. Then leave it be. Laundry Day will definitely get it off you. You'll get flayed in the process. Most armour isn't physically attached. That one is.

beats.headline: The bard potions are brewing
beats.text: Tipid warned me before Carl asked. A karaoke guild, and the needle has to stay in the green for the whole song. So yes, the bard potion. It is brewing now. It will not be ready until just before the next race.

beats.headline: A soul returned, a mind still gone
beats.text: Carl's driver goes down Gingered, unconscious, health bleeding out, and he messages me in a panic. Listen. Did you kill the mob that did it? Good. That returns her soul. It does not return her. She needs specialised healing from a cleric, and until she gets it she is in a fugue, staring at nothing. Good thing you have a backup driver. Try to keep that one.

beats.headline: The test worked, mostly
beats.text: Believe it or not, the test worked. Samantha can't die and she's not what you'd call a reliable subject, so we ran it again on some sluggalos. It works. There are a few wrinkles, and I'm working on them right now. But listen to me, kid. This is so far off the codex we don't even know the system will let Li Na do it. And if it does, she could still die when your floor collapses. He says he knows. He always says he knows.

beats.headline: Goddamn sapient weapons
beats.text: Okay. We're busy prepping the Li Na exit, but we took a look at Dong. It says Negative ROI. Mistress Tiatha thinks it's really a curse called Separation Anxiety, and if she's right a temple won't do a thing. We need the sock back, and every coin he lost. The sock went for Bucket Boy and got teleported by the safe room rules, and it's probably in Hungry Eyes in somebody else's hands. That's what sapient weapons do. They use an owner up and move on. I didn't see this one coming. Its stupid origin story hid it.

beats.headline: Two hundred plants under glass
beats.text: Li Na's dread cactus is steady, one bloom. Ronit, the druid, has worked out something simpler for the rest: every crawler who went through gets a small potted plant tied to their life. Wilts or turns to dust, they're dead. Blooms, they got out. I had to build a glass terrarium for the lot because the sluggalos were eyeing them. Two hundred-some pots in the guildhall common room. It's the only way we'll know. Even the showrunners can't see in there.

beats.headline: Mimics, and safe words
beats.text: Listen. If the Desperado Club is infested, you can't go back. Mimics are almost impossible to root out; the whole place needs fumigating. They dodge most detection spells, like one of Carl's level fifteen traps, all but invisible. They can mimic a crawler, and the system labels them a crawler right up until you catch one. So you all devise safe words, and you quiz each other every day from here. I'm not asking.

beats.headline: An animistic spirit
beats.text: Welcome to the eleventh floor. I'm not going to be much physical help to you. I'm an animistic spirit: no body of my own, I occupy objects. Not my first time as one. Donut hears racist. Animistic, Donut. I can still talk in chat, so we do classes. Comeback Kid gives you every old skill, leveled up, and every old penalty with it; I'd have to research it and we don't have time. The Gurkha one comes with pet and mercenary skills. Take that.

beats.headline: He is the table
beats.text: I'm the table. Samantha is sitting on me. Donut, you're standing right next to me. I can hear all of you, but I can't answer out loud unless I move into something with a mouth, and I'm not good at moving yet. Won't be in a few hours, either. We just had to fight a table, she says. I know. It freaks me out too. I feel like I gotta pee. Carl, the backpack is done. It's on your crafting table.

beats.headline: Safe rooms are not safe
beats.text: The splooge is a type of potion, but it's treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules don't apply. As for the pig's nipple, I don't know how to respond to that, Carl. What you need to know: we're okay. Game guides appear to be immune. Safe rooms are not safe from these nine-tier attacks. Bucket Boy got hit, and Mistress Tiatha healed him in time.
